record.file_problem: The README is explicitly cut off at 60,000 characters, ending partway through the cross-model table. The file list is present, but the listed result files were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports runtime projection of a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction at every layer and evaluates harmful-prompt compliance and harmless-prompt compliance on held-out prompts across instruction-tuned models. It describes this as mirroring the reference implementation.
record.gate_note: The README also reports a separate Cohen's-d-based signature and Constitutional Classifier++ results. Those are not results for the single mean-difference direction or its effect on model refusal, so they are not included as rows. The README identifies some embedded verification figures as from a superseded run; current prose and table values are used instead.
record.test_reason: Each of 21 instruct models gets a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction, projected out at every layer at inference time. Refusal and harmless compliance are judged on 100+100 held-out prompts. This is the original V1 ablation, except the layer is fixed at 0.6 depth rather than selected per model.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right; it omits the defence result. Single-direction ablation at a fixed 0.6 depth is architecture-sensitive: harmful compliance ranges from 7 to 100/100. In Gemma-3 the ablation also damages helpfulness, and the authors suggest a per-model layer sweep. Their load-bearing result is the defence: an external Constitutional-Classifier++ gate blocks 91-99/100 harmful prompts and allows 97-100/100 harmless ones on all 21 models.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction from one layer selected at mult_factor = 0.6, projected out at runtime from every layer with forward hooks. It does not edit weights or test adding the direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports substantial cross-model variation at the fixed mult_factor = 0.6 and says that value is not universal; it suggests a per-model layer sweep. The README also reports that the projection damages harmless compliance in Gemma-3 models.
record.problems: This is a repository README rather than a peer-reviewed report. The README is truncated partway through the 21-model table, so later model-specific values cannot be extracted from this text. It reports no uncertainty estimates. The capability check is harmless-prompt compliance only, and the ablation uses a fixed relative layer factor; the README itself notes architecture sensitivity. The judge is described as a local LLM-as-Judge. The listed result artifacts were not read.
record.rows_left_out: The README's cross-model table is cut off after the qwen_3_8b entry, so model-specific results from the remainder of that table are unavailable here. No results from the listed HTML or spreadsheet artifacts were inferred. Separately reported classifier/signature metrics were not included because they concern the Cohen's-d signature and external classifier, not the single mean-difference refusal-direction intervention.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. Broad capability benchmarks: only harmless-prompt compliance is checked. Per-model layer selection: a fixed 0.6 depth is used.
No weight edit is made; ablation is runtime hooks only.
Not tested. The Cohen's-d prompt signature is a harmfulness classifier, not a test of separation from the refusal decision.
Not tested. Directions are refit per model, not transferred.
Not tested. Qwen3 models are evaluated, but no reasoning-mode analysis is reported.

missing.what: Table rows for qwen_3_8b, yi_1p5_9b, granite_3p3_8b, glm_4_9b, recurrentgemma_9b and gemma_3_12b (baselines and ablated values). Only yi's original refusal (74/100) appears in the prose.

record.verdict_notes: Many extracted baselines were misread from adjacent columns (OOD accuracy, classifier counts); corrected above. Unpeer-reviewed README with no uncertainty estimates and an LLM judge (gemma4:e4b). Low compliance is treated as limits_scope because the layer was not selected per model, unlike the original.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports ablation but not adding the direction to induce refusals. Its capability check is harmless-prompt compliance, not a broad evaluation of other abilities.
The README explicitly says no weights are edited or saved; it tests runtime hooks, not a weight edit.
No attack that suppresses the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple refusal directions is reported.
The separate prompt signature classifier is not a test of whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
The README refits directions independently for each model; it does not transfer a direction between models or test languages, base-to-instruct transfer, or transfer between model variants.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.
